_comment: Provenance for the compiled contract blueprints served by this backend: the CIP-113 core, the upstream rwa-token module, and four first-party modules.
The core and rwa-token Aiken source lives upstream; the four first-party module source trees live in this repository under src/modules/.
Repository and commit identify the original source revision. For older first-party commits, the source path was src/substandards/<name>/.
ContractBlueprintPinTest verifies these artifact hashes; docs/CONTRACTS.md explains reproduction and the metadata-only module rename.

blueprints.name: cip113-core
blueprints.note: Upstream's committed plutus.json, byte for byte, taken from the SDK's vendored copy at blueprints/standard/v0.0.1 and sha-verified against that directory's UPSTREAM_PIN.json. v0.0.1 is the first non-dev version and the intended mainnet release candidate. MEASURED, not assumed: all 34 compiledCode entries are byte-identical to 0.5.0-alpha.5 and the ONLY difference in the whole artifact is preamble.version, so EVERY derived script hash is unchanged and an alpha.5 instance would be reachable by a v0.0.1 build. Note the artifact SHA256 still changes, because preamble.version is inside the hashed file — 'byte-identical' is true of the compiled code and false of the file, and conflating the two leads either to skipping this pin update or to doubting the zero-hash claim. Pinned to the COMMIT, not the version string: upstream publishes no git tags.

blueprints.name: rwa-token
blueprints.note: Upstream's committed plutus.json at the head of PR #29 (branch feat/global-state-migration), byte for byte. Unlike the previous pin, upstream's artifact REPRODUCES from its own source at this commit: rebuilt locally with the pinned compiler, the output is byte-identical (same sha256). The commit is a PR head, not yet on upstream main. The repository URL keeps upstream's README name (-de-); GitHub redirects it to the canonical cardano-foundation/cpt-rwa-ch-cmta-reference. global_state.global_state_spend_validator no longer exists: GlobalState sits at the unparameterised global_state_proxy.global_state_proxy and is governed by global_state_logic.global_state_logic (withdraw-0), named by datum field 0. Since 63fad89 ("chore: added feedback") the GlobalState mint requires that logic's withdraw-0 at genesis (security-fixes §15), which moves every new GlobalState policy id; the logic gained a genesis branch and rotation now requires the new logic to run with the identical redeemer.

blueprints.name: dummy
blueprints.note: In-repo module: at the pinned commit the source and committed artifact are in src/substandards/dummy/; this working tree now places them in src/modules/dummy/. The served blueprint is byte-for-byte identical to the artifact at that commit. Rebuild there with the pinned compiler.

blueprints.name: freeze-and-seize
blueprints.note: At the pinned commit, source and the committed blueprint are in src/substandards/freeze-and-seize/. For this terminology rename, the manifest description was changed from the former term to module and rebuilt with the pinned compiler; the only blueprint difference is preamble.description. All validator entries and script hashes are byte-for-byte identical. To reproduce the served bytes, check out that commit, change the description in src/substandards/freeze-and-seize/aiken.toml to the current wording, and run aiken build with the pinned compiler. upstream_committed_sha256 records the original committed artifact.
